items.prompt: Which word describes the elephant? 'The huge elephant drinks water.'
hints: A describing word tells us more about a noun.
What is the elephant like?
Look at the word just before elephant.
items.explanation: Huge describes the elephant. It tells us its size.

items.prompt: Which describing word fits ice best?
hints: Think about how ice feels.
Imagine holding an ice cube.
Which word is about temperature?

options.why: Fluffy is for things like kittens.
Ice does not make a loud sound.

items.prompt: Sort the describing words. Size or colour?
hints: Size words tell how big or small.
Colour words name a colour.
Start with tiny. Is it a size or a colour?
items.explanation: Tiny, huge and tall are size words. Green, purple and pink are colour words.

items.prompt: Choose all the describing words. 'A fluffy white cat sat on a soft mat.'
hints: Three words are right.
Describing words tell us more about the cat and the mat.
Ask: what is the cat like? What is the mat like?
items.explanation: Fluffy and white describe the cat. Soft describes the mat.

items.prompt: Add -er to compare. 'A bus is big. A plane is ___.'
hints: Add -er to compare two things.
Big is a short word with one vowel.
Double the last letter before you add -er.
items.explanation: Big becomes bigger. We double the g before adding -er.

items.prompt: Which word tells how something feels when you touch it?
hints: Think about your fingers.
Each word goes with a different sense.
Which word could describe a pebble in your hand?
items.explanation: Smooth tells us how something feels when we touch it.

items.prompt: Which describing word fits best? 'The lemon tastes ___.'
hints: Think about the sense of taste.
Lemons make your face scrunch up.
Which word is about taste?

items.prompt: Match each thing to the best describing word.
hints: Think about how each thing looks, feels or sounds.
Do the ones you are sure about first.
Start with thunder. What do you hear?
items.explanation: A rock is hard, honey is sticky, thunder is loud and a pillow is soft.

items.prompt: Ana is tall. Ben is taller. Cara is the tallest. Who is the tallest?
hints: -er compares two people.
-est means more than all the others.
Find the name that goes with the -est word.
items.explanation: Tallest means taller than everyone else, so Cara is the tallest.

options.why: Ana is tall, but the others are taller.
Ben is taller than Ana, but he is not the tallest.
The words tell us they are different.

items.prompt: Add -est to fast. 'This is the ___ car in the race.'
hints: -est compares more than two things.
Fast does not change before the ending.
Write fast, then add the ending.

items.prompt: Which sentence paints the best picture?
hints: Look for describing words.
Which sentence helps you see the boat?
Count the describing words in each sentence.
items.explanation: Old, wooden and calm help us picture the boat and the sea.

options.text: The old wooden boat floated on the calm sea.
The boat was on the sea.
options.why: This is correct, but it has no describing words.
This is a fact with no detail.

items.prompt: Which word is NOT a describing word?
hints: Three words describe a person.
One word is an action.
Try each one in: a ___ friend.
items.explanation: Jump is a doing word. Brave, kind and funny are describing words.

options.why: Funny describes a person or a thing.

items.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence.
hints: Start with the word that has a capital letter.
The describing words go before kite.
Size usually comes before colour.
items.explanation: I have a big red kite. In English, size words usually come before colour words.

items.prompt: Which word fits? 'My bag is heavy, but your bag is even ___.'
hints: You are comparing two bags.
Use the -er ending.
Heavy ends in y. Change the y to i first.
items.explanation: Heavy becomes heavier. The y changes to i before -er.

options.why: When a word ends in y, change the y to i.
We add -er to a word like heavy.
Heaviest is for more than two things.

items.prompt: Which word is the opposite of smallest?
hints: Smallest ends with -est.
The opposite should also end with -est.
Think: small and big are opposites.
items.explanation: Biggest is the opposite of smallest. Both end with -est.

options.why: Tiniest means the same as smallest.

items.prompt: Which group of words could describe a kitten?
hints: Picture a kitten in your mind.
All three words in the group must fit.
Which group could describe something soft and little?
items.explanation: A kitten can be fluffy, playful and small.

items.prompt: Read: 'The sky was dark and the wind howled.' What kind of day was it?
hints: Look at the describing words.
A dark sky and a howling wind go together.
What weather has dark clouds and strong wind?
items.explanation: A dark sky and a howling wind show it was a stormy day.

options.why: Sunny days are bright, not dark.
A calm day has gentle wind.
Still means there is no wind.

items.prompt: Which describing word tells the number? 'Three small ducks swim.'
hints: Describing words can tell size, colour or number.
Which word answers: how many?
Count the ducks in the sentence.
items.explanation: Three tells us how many ducks. Small tells us the size.
